Warning: Spoilers ahead for _Doctor Who_ season 15, episode 4, "Lucky Day."[**_Doctor Who_**](https://screenrant.com/db/tv-show/doctor-who/) season 15, episode 4, "Lucky Day," introduces Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark and connects him to a key piece of lore from _Doctor Who_ season 14, episode 4, "73 Yards." The piece of worldbuilding in question is the Albion Party, a fictitious right-wing UK political body. Fronted by Roger ap Gwilliam (Aneurin Barnard), **the Albion Party took an extremist stance on some very sensitive subjects**, including nuclear war. [Ruby's alternate timeline in "73 Yards"](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-season-14-episode-4-ending-explained-73-yards-ruby-timeline/) reveals that the divisive political figure stood down thanks to something that was whispered to him on stage by a future version of Ruby.

The Albion Party received more references toward the [end of _Doctor Who_ season 14](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-season-14-ending-explained/), but has since remained on the outskirts of the show's lore. "Lucky Day" doesn't exactly bring the organization to the foreground again, but its origin story is briefly mentioned when [_Doctor Who_'s new UNIT team](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-unit-team-members-explained/) is running a background check on one of its employees. As an addition to the catalog of [_Doctor Who_'s Doctor-lite episodes](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-lite-episodes-ranked/), **"Lucky Day" serves as a sort of prequel to "73 Yards,"** but is more of a spiritual successor that shares several elements.

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

The Albion Party Is "Albion TV" In Doctor Who's 2020s Timeline
--------------------------------------------------------------

### An alternate Ruby Sunday has crossed paths with the Albion Party before

Jordan Lang (Kareem Alexander) turns out to be the mole within UNIT who has leaked the names and addresses of the organization's employees to Conrad and his group of conspiracy theorists, known as Think Tank. During the reveal, it's established that Jordan has some worrying interests, including a subscription to Albion TV. In the 2020s, if the Albion Party even exists, it's still in its earliest stages. **It won't be until the 2040s that the service to which Jordan is subscribed exists as an established political party**, which allows Roger ap Gwilliam to run for Prime Minister.

The Albion Party's leader in "73 Yards," Roger ap Gwilliam, is also known by the nickname, Mad Jack.

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

So, **"Lucky Day" essentially gives the Albion Party an origin story** by softly confirming it began as a subscription service for individuals with a political ideology similar to that of Jordan, Conrad, and the other members of Think Tank. Extrapolating from what we know about those associated with the Albion Party, Albion TV likely features programming revolving around nationalism, and even touching on subjects such as a proclivity for nuclear war, which was a strongly implied desire of Roger ap Gwilliam in "73 Yards."

Conrad's Podcast & The Albion Party Are Thematically Connected
--------------------------------------------------------------

### Doctor Who made sure to make the similarities clear

![Image 12: Conrad Clark speaking on his podcast in Doctor Who](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/untitled-2025-05-03t104417-167.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2)

Conrad Clark speaking on his podcast in Doctor Who

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

**Conrad enters the story as a podcast host**. The show flaunts a pro-Doctor message to lure people in, but really, Conrad despises the Doctor. Paradoxically, Conrad ultimately ends up spreading his theory that alien life does not exist, despite meeting the Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) in 2007. The following that Conrad gathers with his deceptive rhetoric is, in his opinion, for the good of the country. He has all of his allies believing that UNIT is a money-grabbing front that was set up by the government to make UK residents pay more tax, and that extraterrestrial life is a myth.

![Image 13: Custom Doctor Who image of Matt Smith as the Eleventh Doctor, Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor, and Jodie Whittaker as the Thirteenth Doctor](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/doctor-who-season-15-revives-a-matt-smith-mystery-that-became-redundant-after-the-timeless-child.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=220&h=182&dpr=2)Related 

##### [Doctor Who Season 15 Revives A Matt Smith Mystery That Became Redundant After The Timeless Child](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-real-name-mystery-matt-smith-season-15-explainer/ "Doctor Who Season 15 Revives A Matt Smith Mystery That Became Redundant After The Timeless Child")

Matt Smith's Eleventh Doctor had an arc that closely addressed one of Doctor Who's biggest mysteries, and "The Well" visits that storyline again.

Posts [10](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-real-name-mystery-matt-smith-season-15-explainer/#threads "Total Posts")

By[Daniel Bibby](https://screenrant.com/author/daniel-bibby/ "Posts by Daniel Bibby")

May 1, 2025

It's quite clear that all Conrad is really after is attention, after "Lucky Day" reveals in the episode's introduction that [Hauer-King's character didn't have the most loving childhood in the world](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-season-15-episode-4-conrad-lie-hint-explainer/). Similarly, Roger ap Gwilliam claims that all of his policies are in the country's best interests, but they ultimately turn out to be incredibly self-serving and satisfy his need for more control and power, potentially even for his bloodlust. In this way, **Conrad's podcast running alongside Albion TV may have contributed to ap Gwilliam's eventual rise to power**.

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

Doctor Who's "Lucky Day" & "73 Yards" Carry Very Similar Messages
-----------------------------------------------------------------

### Pete McTighe penned a brilliant script that intertwines with Russell T. Davies' 2024 story

**Millie Gibson's Ruby Sunday leads both "73 Yards" and "Lucky Day,"** with Gatwa having incredibly muted roles in both installments. As such, the theme of Ruby being left behind by the Doctor is prevalent in the two stories. In each of the two Gibson-led installments, [Ruby is shown trying to adapt to life after traveling in the TARDIS](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-ruby-sunday-companion-ptsd-problem-explainer/), and ending up stepping in to quash the rise of a far-right movement. Neither the villain in "73 Yards" nor "Lucky Day" is particularly conventional for a show like _Doctor Who_, with the problematic figureheads both primarily threatening the UK's safety.

"73 Yards" and "Lucky Day" are both brilliant examples of _Doctor Who_ thriving at grounded storytelling.

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

Although sci-fi serves as a narrative vehicle for both episodes, "73 Yards" and "Lucky Day" are both brilliant examples of _Doctor Who_ thriving at grounded storytelling. They also make it clear that **threats to the Earth within the show's canon aren't always extraterrestrial**, and that humans with loaded agendas can be just as dangerous as a fleet of Daleks or other **_Doctor Who_** villains - just in different ways.

It was written by Pete McTighe, and was directed by Peter Hoar. The episode was released on BBC iPlayer, BBC One, and Disney+ on 3 May 2025. It features the return of companion Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson), who plays a leading role in the episode opposite Conrad Clark (Jonah Hauer-King), with both the Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) and Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu), the series' main leads, only appearing briefly. The episode focuses on Ruby, who begins a relationship with Conrad as she attempts to find her place in the world after leaving the Doctor. When it is revealed that Conrad wants to "expose" UNIT for their goals being "fake", Ruby and Kate Lethbridge-Stewart have to deal with the repercussions of Conrad's actions. The episode was devised by showrunner Russell T Davies, with Davies enlisting McTighe to write the episode. He used the episode to explore Ruby and Kate's characters while also exploring the "the spread of online hatred" and its effects. The episode's monster, the Shreek, was based off of McTighe's childhood fears of dog-like creatures in the dark, with the creature being portrayed via costume and an animatronic head. Filming took place in November 2023 and it was filmed back-to-back with the series premiere. The episode received positive reviews from critics, who highlighted Gibson's performance, the twist regarding Conrad's true identity, and the episode's social commentary, but were more critical of underdeveloped plotlines in the episode, as well as the execution of Conrad as an antagonist. Plot [edit] The Doctor and Belinda arrive on New Year's Day, 2007, and meet eight-year-old Conrad. Following this, Conrad investigates sightings of the Doctor and the TARDIS, seeing a younger Doctor with his then-companion Ruby in 2024, where he is marked as prey by a creature called the Shreek. In 2025, after stopping travelling with the Doctor, Ruby gives Conrad about her encounters with extraterrestrial life an interview on his podcast. They start dating and she gives him an antidote to act against him being marked by the Shreek, which has been recently captured by UNIT. At a weekend away at Conrad's home village, Ruby fears she is in danger and tells Conrad she is suffering from PTSD following her experiences with the Doctor. Two Shreek appear in pursuit of Conrad, who admits he did not take the antidote. Ruby calls UNIT and their leader Kate to the village. The Shreek are revealed to be fake, part of a setup orchestrated by Conrad, whose relationship with Ruby was a ploy, against UNIT. A scandal breaks and Conrad and his followers continue to perpetuate disinformation about the non-existence of aliens, discrediting UNIT. Warning: Spoilers ahead for _Doctor Who_ season 15, episode 4, "Lucky Day."[**_Doctor Who_**](https://screenrant.com/db/tv-show/doctor-who/) season 15, episode 4, "Lucky Day," boasts a narratively dense ending that perfectly reflects the installment's complex subject matter, which can make it difficult to keep up with everything that happens. Although **it's not a sequel to _Doctor Who_ season 14's "73 Yards,"** "Lucky Day" has several big similarities to the 2024 episode, which was also led by Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in place of Ncuti Gatwa's Fifteenth Doctor. There are also a lot of crossovers when it comes to the topics that form the basis of both stories.

Despite the Doctor's muted roles in both, I think the two episodes are some of the finest in [_Doctor Who_'s Disney era](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-season-1-14-40-disney-confusion/) so far. In fact, **the Time Lord taking a backseat in "Lucky Day" is what clears the way for a storyline of this nature** to unfold. Although it's dressed up in certain sci-fi hallmarks, the episode is incredibly grounded for a show like _Doctor Who_ and touches on some real-world issues in a fantastical way. While [_Doctor Who_'s Doctor-lite episodes](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-lite-episodes-ranked/) often focus largely on a companion's plight, "Lucky Day" remembers to address far more.

How Conrad Connects To Doctor Who's "73 Yards" & The Albion Party
-----------------------------------------------------------------

### "Lucky Day" mentions a subscription service called Albion TV

[✕ Remove Ads](https://screenrant.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

"73 Yards" feels like a spiritual predecessor to "Lucky Day," and, at times, even a retroactive sequel. Although [Ruby's alternate timeline in "73 Yards"](https://screenrant.com/doctor-who-season-14-episode-4-ending-explained-73-yards-ruby-timeline/) has now been wiped out due to the return of the Doctor, there's nothing to say that certain events from the future Ruby once lived through won't still happen. Specifically, "Lucky Day" reveals the existence of a right-wing subscription service called Albion TV. In the 2040s shown in "73 Yards," **Prime Minister Roger ap Gwilliam (Aneurin Barnard) was the leader of the Albion Party**, which won the UK General Election.

Albion TV is mentioned as a service that Jordan Lang (Kareem Alexander) subscribes to while the Vlinx (Nicholas Briggs) runs a background check on the traitorous UNIT agent.

While Conrad isn't confirmed to have a direct, canonical connection to the Albion Party, his _Lucky Day_ podcast belongs to the same group as Albion TV, boasting far-right rhetoric, unfounded conspiracy theories, and wild speculation by individuals who are far from experts in their respective fields. Because the ideologies of Albion TV and Conrad's podcast seem to be so similar, it could be that **the attention garnered by Think Tank by those in similar circles resulted in a surge in Albion TV subscribers**, which will eventually lead to the creation of the party that takes Roger ap Gwilliam to power.
